statement: Tom stands 5 dominoes in a line. Each is 3 cm thick, with a 1 cm gap between neighbours. How long is the whole line, end to end?

choices.misconception: I added the 5 dominoes and forgot the gaps between them.
I added one gap of 1 cm for the whole line instead of one between every two dominoes.
I put a gap after every domino, even after the last one.
I put a gap between the dominoes and also one at each end of the line.

hints: Draw the 5 dominoes and mark the gaps.
Gaps only go between neighbours, so there is one fewer gap than dominoes. A quick sketch shows exactly how many gaps there are. Then add the dominoes and the gaps.
The 5 dominoes make 15 cm. Drawing them shows 4 gaps, one between each pair of neighbours. Add the gaps.

solutions.reliable: The dominoes are $5 \times 3 = 15$ cm thick altogether. Between 5 dominoes there are 4 gaps, so the gaps add 4 cm. The line is $15 + 4 = 19$ cm long. The idea to keep: in a row of things, there is one gap fewer than things.
solutions.elegant: Think of each of the first 4 dominoes with the gap behind it: that is 4 cm each, so 16 cm. The last domino has no gap behind it and adds 3 cm, making 19 cm.

whyOnTest: Gaps between objects are a classic off-by-one, and drawing the row is the reliable way to count them.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
